unresolved.title: Summum Bonum
unresolved.author: Robert Fludd
unresolved.query: Summum bonum magiae cabalae alchymiae fratrum Roseae Crucis
unresolved.epithet: Fludd's defence of the Rose Cross and its magic
unresolved.summary: Fludd's reply to Mersenne under a pseudonym, defending magic, cabala and alchemy and the Brotherhood of the Rose Cross — the source of the famous rose-and-cross engraving 'Dat Rosa Mel Apibus'.

unresolved.title: Medicina Catholica
unresolved.author: Robert Fludd
unresolved.epithet: A weather-glass of the winds and the body
unresolved.summary: Fludd's macrocosm-microcosm medicine, in which the health of the body answers to the winds, stars and archangels of the greater world — his fullest picture of man mirrored in the cosmos.

unresolved.title: L'Homme de désir
unresolved.author: Louis-Claude de Saint-Martin
unresolved.epithet: The unknown philosopher's song of the fallen soul
unresolved.summary: Saint-Martin's lyrical meditations on the desire that draws the fallen human being back toward its divine source — the devotional heart of the Martinist path he taught after breaking with ceremonial magic.

unresolved.title: The Immortality of the Soul
unresolved.author: Henry More
unresolved.query: Immortality of the Soul Henry More
unresolved.epithet: The Cambridge Platonist's proof of the spirit-world
unresolved.summary: More's demonstration of the soul's immortality and of a graded world of spirits and 'spissitude' — the Cambridge Platonist metaphysics that gave later psychical research its philosophical warrant.

unresolved.title: Das Geheimnis der göttlichen Sophia
unresolved.author: Gottfried Arnold
unresolved.epithet: The mystery of the divine Wisdom
unresolved.summary: Arnold's treatise on the divine Sophia, the heavenly Wisdom of Böhme and the Philadelphians — the scholarly Pietist's gathering of the whole Sophia tradition into one book.

unresolved.title: L'Économie divine
unresolved.author: Pierre Poiret
unresolved.epithet: A whole system of mystical divinity
unresolved.summary: Poiret's seven-volume system of divine economy — the philosophical Cartesian-turned-mystic who edited Antoinette Bourignon and gathered the quietist and theosophic currents of his century.

unresolved.title: The Spirit of Prayer
unresolved.author: William Law
unresolved.epithet: Böhme Englished by a master of prose
unresolved.summary: Law's dialogues on the birth of God in the soul, the fruit of his late immersion in Böhme — the most eloquent English statement of the theosophical mysticism he spent his last years expounding.

unresolved.title: Via Lucis
unresolved.author: Jan Amos Comenius
unresolved.epithet: The way of light: a pansophic college of nations
unresolved.summary: Comenius's plan for the universal spread of light through a pansophic college, a universal language and a reformed learning — the eirenic, Rosicrucian-tinged utopia of the great educator.

unresolved.title: La Lumière du Monde
unresolved.author: Antoinette Bourignon
unresolved.epithet: The visionary who gathered her own disciples
unresolved.summary: Bourignon's account of her inner light and revelations — the Flemish mystic whose claim to a direct divine illumination drew a following across Protestant Europe and scandalised its churches.

unresolved.title: Earths in the Universe
unresolved.author: Emanuel Swedenborg
unresolved.epithet: The spirits of the other planets
unresolved.summary: Swedenborg's report of his conversations with the spirits of the moon and the planets — the strangest of his shorter works, and a favourite of the later occult and science-fiction imagination.

unresolved.title: Aurora, or the Day-Spring
unresolved.author: Jacob Böhme
unresolved.epithet: The first, unfinished dawn of Böhme's vision
unresolved.summary: Böhme's first book, the ecstatic and unfinished Aurora, in John Sparrow's English — the work whose seizure by the church first made the shoemaker of Görlitz notorious.
